column3: And the loud over-the-top guy that loves being the center of attention ended up having a knack for politics.
Who could have POSSIBLY guessed those outcomes?
CAIN: Hey now, I like to think me turning out like this is pretty surprising.
AYA: I mean, you being good at the job isn't surprising.
You actually sticking to it instead of running away when it gets stressful is, though.
CAIN: Ice cold...
TAKA: Oh, uh, that's...
CAIN: Don't worry about it, she only teases me with love.
AYA: Yeah, he's a pretty okay brother I guess, may as well actually be nice from time to time.
TAKA: Oh I'm glad.
Anyway, it was really nice to see you both...
I'm glad you're both doing so great.
CAIN: I'm sure in ten years you'll be in a similar boat to us, doing whatever works for you.
Remember, be like Bigglesworth.
Even if you wake up in the morning, look in the mirror, and don't like the person you see?
Self love doesn't happen in a day,
But if you think you're garbage,
Just make sure you're a garbage CAN.
Keep that up and you'll start liking the person you see, just like everyone else likes you.
AYA: I write songs for a living and I still think the lines Cain comes up with are corny as hell.
But he's not wrong, you're pretty cool, Taka.
AYA: Hey \PN, hey Elias.
ELIAS: Hello to both of you.
You appear to be doing very well.
ELIAS: I can only imagine that if the music's creator is this enthusiastic,
That must shine through in the final product.
This Garbodor did not know how to battle?
I don't think I have ever encountered a Pokémon that does not know a single move...
CAIN: Oh no, I mean as in, like using Pokéballs.
ELIAS: I... see?
And you had this... talking Pokémon run for office?
CAIN: Listen, Biggles is a great guy, you'd know if you met him.
AYA: ...Anyway, even something silly like this, Cain decides to dedicate all his time and attention to.
ELIAS: I'm sorry I...
You're saying this Pokémon managed to actually win the mayoral race?
That must have been a remarkable slogan, I genuinely would like to know.
ELIAS: It is certainly...
Snappy.
ELIAS: Many brilliant things in life start with a fluke.
Perhaps all good things.
A fluke is little more than my Lord's will, after all, is it not?
It sounds to me like you've both managed to find exactly the path that is best for you.
ELIAS: ...
ELIAS: Ah, I see, this must be the 'sibling banter' I have heard much about...
Well, I am happy you both seem quite so close, family is important.
I do hope I can one day feel the same with what little family I still have left...
But he's not wrong.
I'm sure if you put the right work in, you can get the right results out.
I'll see you both; I'm sure you'll do great back in your time.
AYA: Hey again, how's it going?
Enjoying seeing how everyone is doing after so long?
Must be pretty surreal for you, I bet.
It'll probably be even weirder when you go back to your time and look at everyone, knowing how we'll turn out.
Well, how we might turn out, at least.
Maybe your presence will change things?
I know you made a difference to my life when you were here, so maybe you'll continue to do so.
Hey, but whenever our band starts getting big?
You better buy tickets to every show.
Maybe one extra dedicated fan will help me get comfortable with it all even faster than I did.
And thanks for coming back, really.
Cain really missed you.
We all did.
Even if it's only brief, it's lovely to see you.
BENNETT: \PN, hello.
Shelly always said you would be back.
And I tend to trust her word.
Whether it's about the New World, Legendary Pokémon, or anything else really, she tends to know what she's talking about.
But you'd probably expect me to say that.
I've never met a Bug Type specialist I didn't get along with.
...Well, except that cop or whatever he was from Aevium.
I swear, you try to buy parts to repair your Genesect's cannon one singular time...
And a lot of people start getting very agitated.
I can't even buy fertilizer for the plants anymore; Laura has to handle that!
BENNETT: ...Apologies.
But I digress,
That little incident aside, my life has been remarkably peaceful since moving into the manor with Laura.
It's nice that we are near enough Spinel, that it's easy for both our families to visit if they want.
...Although I'm quite content, visitors or no.
Laura's company is already so wonderful, after all.
LAURA: \PN, Elias, how delightful of you to come and greet us.
LAURA: \PN, Taka, how delightful of you to come and greet us.
Amaria was just seeking some of our expertise,
But we can all say hello while we help.
BENNETT: I'm glad you're both safe, welcome back.
AMARIA: Hi again, I'd love to chat more once I'm done here!
TAKA: Hey again, everyone.
Uh, you all look well.
LAURA: I certainly think so!
Bennett and myself take care of numerous plants and insects, and I find taking care of others is very helpful to yourself.
And Amaria here has recently started doing the same, getting some houseplants of her own!
AMARIA: Yeah, my place was feeling a little empty, so I got a plant to liven it up!
And one turned into two, and two turned into three, and three turned into ten...
I mean, you guys get it, I'm sure.
Anyway, that's actually what I wanted to talk about.
One of my plants has an infestation, you see, and I don't know what to do about it...
LAURA: Oh, how awful!
BENNETT: ...Infestation of what?
AMARIA: I'm not certain, but they're tiny and when I tried to water the plant the other day, I got a little shock?
BENNETT: Sounds like Joltik.
Don't worry, they're a lot less of a problem than you think.
I mean, the plant is probably done for.
But taking care of a few hundred Joltik is remarkably easy, and they're very friendly.
First you need--
Oh, actually, you'll need protectors for any of your power outlets.
They're small enough to get inside and chew on wires, that can be a problem...
Any exposed wiring is an issue really. If your computer is higher end, you might need--
LAURA: Bennett!
She was asking about the plant, not all of the Joltik.
I understand your excitement, but you should remember what people asked for help with when you're giving your help.
BENNETT: Oh, right.
Sorry, Amaria. I got ahead of myself.
Laura can take this one.
AMARIA: Oh, it's okay, I understand getting excited...
LAURA: Right, well, Joltik are actually not a problem for the plant at all!
In fact, the small electric charge they give off encourages growth!
And they aren't actually interested in eating the plant, they just want the water.
So you need to make sure to water the plant extra.
Oh, while they pose no danger to the plant, there is some to you.
You'll need to water from a safe distance,
Make sure the plant is nowhere near any electronics...
Make sure no people or Pokémon touch the plant...
If you need to repot, wear heavy protective gear...
...There's something else, I think.
BENNETT: Don't keep the plant in your kitchen, you don't want Joltik getting in your food.
LAURA: Ah, how could I forget!
Oh, and of course if there's anything like a hot tub or pool in your home, you don't want Joltik anywhere near that.
BENNETT: Or if there's a lake or pond nearby outside, you probably keep the plant away from a window too.
LAURA: Right, yes, and then there's...
AMARIA: ...I knew I should have asked...
I mean, literally anybody else about this.
Hey, sorry for dragging you two into this.
I just wanted to know how to get those Joltik off of my plant...
TAKA: It's fine, really.
I uh, I get it.
I remember asking Terra for computer help one time back in Meteor,
And I ended up getting a four hour live reading of a very bad fanfiction.
Learned pretty quick to ask someone else for computer help after that.
...Starting to think I had a pretty weird childhood.
AMARIA: Well, I'm glad things are less weird for everyone now.
I mean, in the scheme of things at least.
...You two should probably sneak off, I don't think they'll be done any time soon.
Good to see you again though, and welcome back.
TAKA: Uh, yeah, you too.
Come on \PN, I think this is enough Joltik facts for a lifetime...
ELIAS: Bennett, Laura.
It is nice to see you are both well despite any...  unpleasantness I may have had a hand in.
LAURA: It was so long ago, Elias, and I told you even then that there are no hard feelings.
None of us are on the Elite Four anymore anyway.
So in that sense, the situation has simply resolved itself, has it not?
BENNETT: Your positivity, optimism, and speed of forgiveness still amaze me even after ten years, Laura.
But she is right that these things were a long time ago for us, El.
Any ill will has long since passed.
ELIAS: Well, that is lovely to hear.
Whatever the circumstances, you both did a fine job as Elite Four.
And as I said, I am glad you both look to be well.
As do you, Amaria.
LAURA: I agree, we all do look well!
ELIAS: There is no need to apologize.
Their passion is admirable.
I must admit, I may be guilty of going on similar tangents in sermons when people ask me questions at times.
Given the correct topic, the majority of my colleagues back in Meteor were much the same.
...Although I do concede perhaps the goals bringing us together made the people drawn to the group...
Less than normal.
ELIAS: While that does sound awfully rude...
I must admit, I have spent enough time around Bennett to already know...
Far more facts about Bug Pokémon than I ever wished to.
...If we say "Hello" again later, I'm sure they won't mind.
BENNETT: Right, obviously they'll get agitated without the expensive, mineral-rich soils.
LAURA: Oh, that goes without saying.
But not too mineral-rich!
If one of them evolves, the plant and your home and probably you are in quite a bit of trouble!
BENNETT: Yes, although Galvantula are quite soft...
LAURA: They are!
Should we get another?
LAURA: Hello again, \PN!
Apologies, I must have gotten distracted and forgotten to say goodbye after our prior conversation.
It's lovely that you're back, truly.
These days, everything is lovely.
Bennett and I quit the Elite Four and have been tending to our plants and flowers together at the manor.
Charlotte visits quite regularly.
Saphira stops by from time to time.
Even Serra and Luna say hello when they're free!
It's a lovely life we live, because we live it in a lovely world.
Much of that is thanks to Shelly, but I won't forget your contribution too.
In saving the region, you laid the groundwork for........
Everything, I guess!
All of this.
So from the bottom of my heart, I thank you.
For helping make a world where me and my sisters can live so happily.
AMARIA: After listening to Bennett and Laura's advice, I have decided,
To give them the plant, and get a new one.
But enough about that, I have spoken about it far too much already.
Ten years is a long time and I like to think I spent it well.
I could probably ramble on about what I've been doing and in what ways my life has changed.
But really, I think there's only one way it's changed that matters.
I'm happy now.
NOEL: He's trying his best, although I wish he'd stop telling people I'm some kind of divine gift to artistry.
Samson approached me the other day, saying he heard about me from dad.
Wanted to commission me to make some kind of bright, colorful, extravagant engagement ring.
It's not like I can't make it, but I prefer to work in my own style.
I know he's just trying to be supportive, but I don't want people to get the wrong idea about my work.
RADOMUS: My my, do I hear footsteps approach?
Our guests of honor, perhaps?
NOEL: ...Here we go again, I suppose.
RADOMUS: \PN! Taka!
It is wonderful to see you both returned.
And of course, what better way to welcome the guests of honor than with a gift!
The gift of a personal meeting with the greatest artist in all of Reborn--
Nay, all of the world!
NOEL: ...Dad, I told you to stop saying that.
TAKA: You're an artist now?
...I thought chess was your whole thing?
RADOMUS: No, no, no!
Wrong on all counts, I'm afraid.
Firstly, I haven't played chess in years-- I switched to a far more fitting pursuit for my new lifestyle.
Secondly, I am not the artist; it's my darling son here!
NOEL: ...
NOEL: Sure, fine.
Hey, good to see you again. It's good that you're safe.
...Shelly always said you were gonna be fine and you'd show up again, though, so I wasn't worried.
TAKA: Hey... I like your new look, it's pretty funky.
Suits an artist.
So uh, how'd that even happen?
NOEL: It's no big deal, Shelly and I met a Xerneas one time and it...
Well, I had a new appreciation for color, so I started to paint.
And I didn't limit myself to just oils on a canvas.
And some people seemed to like my work, so I kept doing it.
RADOMUS: 'Some people seemed to like' it?
That doesn't even begin to cover your success!
RADOMUS: From the finest galleries in Kalos...
...To the most exclusive resorts in Sinnoh...
Noel's art is on display in some of the most prestigious places around the world!
Why, just last year, he set the record for the most money a living artist has ever sold a single piece for!
NOEL: ...I still don't think that should count when you just showed up to an art show,
Which I didn't even tell you was happening,
And outbid the next guy by a factor of ten.
RADOMUS: Can you blame me?
What better thing to spend my fortune on than an original piece by such a brilliant young artist,
That I can display proudly in my home!
NOEL: ...Didn't you steal that whole fortune from his dad?
RADOMUS: ...
TAKA: ...
RADOMUS: Anyway!
Time travel, how fascinating!
You must tell me everything!
NOEL: Sorry about him.
After things settled down he decided it was his mission in life to be the 'best father ever', whatever that means.
...He's a little much.
TAKA: Must be nice to...
Uh, never mind.
The time travel was all right, we met some interesting people...
You said you don't play chess anymore?
RADOMUS: Yes, yes. I am a lover of strategy and mindgames, I always thought chess was the perfect game for me.
But it can be so solitary, can it not?
Hardly an appropriate way for a family man to spend his time.
Friends, you are looking at the world champion...
RADOMUS: Of Monopoly!
NOEL: You keep saying so, but that title still doesn't exist.
RADOMUS: Ah, my brilliant son, always so sharp.
It is a title that exists in my heart!
And once I get enough participants to set up a world championship, it shall exist to the world!
NOEL: ...Let me know if you ever need anything, \PN.
I owe you a lot.
You too, Taka.
...Even though that feels more like my father's debts than mine.
TAKA: I'll keep that in mind.
And uh, enjoy your...
Family time?
NOEL: ...Yeah.
All things considered, I always do.
Our guest of honor, perhaps?
And not just footsteps, but the slithering of a snake too.
Perhaps our guest has company of their own.
RADOMUS: \PN!
It is wonderful to see you returned.
I see that you are also here, Elias.
ELIAS: Radomus.
You've aged horribly.
RADOMUS: Why, I was about to say the same thing, my dear ex-employee.
It looks like it's been ten years for you, too.
Today is your lucky day, however!
For someone so old that they look mere moments from death, it must be rare to be afforded such a wonderful opportunity.
The opportunity of a personal meeting with the greatest artist in all of Reborn--
ELIAS: World Champion of Chess, and now, what, World Champion of Art?
Art suits you, given how creative you are at coming up with lies to explain your stolen wealth.
RADOMUS: Wrong about everything as usual, Elias.
While you are correct that I have moved on from the life of a chessmaster.
I am not the artist-- that would be my darling son here!
Hey, good to see you again \PN. It's good that you're safe.
ELIAS: You have my sincerest congratulations for turning into such a polite young man,
Despite how gravely this man's very existence stacked the odds against you.
You're an artist now?
And some people seemed to like my work so I kept doing it.
ELIAS: That sounds an awful lot like money laundering.
In fact, given that your fortune was entirely stolen from myself and my master, it probably is.
How very like you, thrusting the consequences of your crimes on your child.
RADOMUS: Oh my! What a great day this is, to receive parenting advice from such an esteemed expert!
Although there is something to be said for a simple difference in styles.
After all, my daughter Luna seems to think I'm a wonderful father.
NOEL: ...Let's just leave them to it.
NOEL: Sorry, \PN. Dad is... a lot.
He got really fixated on being the best father possible after things settled down and...
Well, now I guess he has all that energy to channel into... whatever is going on over there.
RADOMUS: You know, I always felt it would be unfair to just fight you, given how old and frail you are.
But given the ten years, we're about the same age now, so bring it.
ELIAS: Please, you couldn't fight your way out of a wet paper bag.
Your style is no doubt more like kicking me when my back is turned.
NOEL: He even stopped playing chess, you know.
Decided now he was a family man, he needed a family hobby.
The title doesn't exist, but he calls himself the World Champion of Monopoly now...
ELIAS: Oh, and what a FINE parent you are!
So incompatible with your own child you had to change everything about yourself just to bond?
RADOMUS: My deepest apologies I'm not pompous enough to know how to say this in the old language, but,
Those in glass houses shouldn't throw stones, Elias.
NOEL: I'm glad he tries to understand me, at least.
Even if his brand of supportive can be a little...  intense.
It's nice to have him around, even if he's embarrassing.
...It's nice you're back too. Even being confident you would return, it's good that it finally happened.
RADOMUS: LOOK AT ME, I'M ELIAS.
I'M SO REPUGNANT THAT THE IDEA SOMEBODY COULD BE SELFLESS ENOUGH TO TREAT ME WELL IS TOTALLY ALIEN!
SO MUCH SO THAT I CONVINCED MYSELF A RANDOM YOUTH IS ARCEUS BECAUSE THAT'S THE ONLY EXPLANATION!
ELIAS: Well I never...
WELL, MY NAME IS RADOMUS!
I SPENT SO LONG SPOUTING PSEUDO- PHILOSOPHICAL NONSENSE EVERYONE THOUGHT I WAS SOME KIND OF INTELLECTUAL.
SO I JUST LIED AND TOLD THEM I WAS A CHESSMASTER.
I'M NOT EVEN VERY GOOD AT CHESS, BUT NOBODY CAN STAND MY COMPANY LONG ENOUGH TO PLAY A GAME TO FIND OUT!
NOEL: ...Hey, let's get some tea or something.
They're not exactly young men; all that yelling will tire them out eventually...
...Probably.
\PN and Noel proceeded to have a lovely cup of tea at the café.
They discussed his art, time travel, and much more.
When they returned, Radomus and Elias were indeed out of breath from all the shouting and yelling.
ELIAS: Well... I have... many people I'd rather greet.
I will talk to you later, my Lord.
RADOMUS: Good riddance...
Ahem, but where are my manners.
Even with the downside of the company you have brought, your return is nonetheless a good thing, \PN.
Welcome back, once more.
NOEL: Yeah, welcome back.
Thanks for everything, too.
RADOMUS: To think, all the time I lost being separated from my son.
I want nothing more than to take back all those lost years, but I will make do with making up for it instead.
I struggled to truly understand him for quite some time but...
He seems to crack a smile at my antics more often these days.
So I can only hope I'm doing something right.
TAKA: Oh, \PN, hey.
I was just saying hi to Luna here.
LUNA: Taka was telling me all about your journey through time, how fascinating.
But where are my manners, time travel must be exhausting!
Would you like a refreshment?
